// name: Scoped @applyy (two y's) per the naming standard; the repo folder stays applyyy and is NOT renamed.
name: @applyy/master-ingest
// version: Workspace-internal only; nothing here is ever published to a registry.
// private: This package's fixtures and callers carry real resume content — an accidental `pnpm publish` must be impossible.
// type: ESM only. The reconciler has to be importable by a Deno Edge Function, the Node worker and the browser console alike, and Deno cannot consume CommonJS.
// exports: Source-only export map pointing at .ts, exactly like resume-template. There is deliberately NO build step: a build would create a second, stale copy of the function that decides whether a node id survives, and the whole point of this package is that that decision is made in exactly one place.
// types: Redundant with exports for modern resolvers; kept for editors that still read this field.
// files: Only src ships if this is ever packed.
// scripts.typecheck: tsc is a checker only in this repo — noEmit is inherited from tsconfig.base.json.
// scripts.test: The glob is REQUIRED. `node --test test` (a bare directory) fails on Node 24 with MODULE_NOT_FOUND, and that error reads exactly like missing fixtures, which is how a previous session lost time to it.
// dependencies: shared-types owns MasterProfile and NodeId. This package reconciles those shapes and must never re-declare them: a local copy of MasterProfile would let the reconciler carry ids forward under a shape the database no longer stores.
// devDependencies: @types/node is needed by the TESTS ONLY (node:test, node:assert). src/ uses no Node API at all — not even crypto, which is why mintId is injected rather than ambient. typescript for standalone type-checking; the floor is 5.8 because tsconfig.base.json sets erasableSyntaxOnly, which 5.6/5.7 reject as an unknown option. NOTE: these explanations live at the TOP level because pnpm validates dependency names and rejects a "// x" pseudo-key inside dependencies with ERR_PNPM_INVALID_DEPENDENCY_NAME — the same trap as TS5025 inside compilerOptions.
